## Upgrade from 0.3.1

**0.4.0 requires a coordinated upgrade. Stop all older writers and retention workers before
migrating, then deploy matching API, engine, and store artifacts across the fleet.** Do not
run 0.3.1 and 0.4.0 nodes against the migrated database at the same time.

This requirement applies to the transition to the new storage contracts. Future releases
can support rolling upgrades when compatibility has been established for that version pair.

- SQL stores: apply `V007__permanent_idempotency_keys.sql` and
  `V008__priority_ordered_claim_index.sql` before starting 0.4.0 workers. This applies to
  MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server. Keep already-applied migrations unchanged.
- MongoDB: keep older writers stopped while the first upgraded node backfills permanent
  reservations. Verify initialization before starting the remaining fleet. Transactions
  require a replica set or sharded deployment.
- Custom stores: implement the new atomic completion, recurring execution, recurring
  query/count, and permanent-idempotency lookup contracts. Update the engine and store
  implementations together.
- Rollback requires a rehearsed database-and-binary restore, accounting for work performed
  since the backup. Restarting old binaries alone can bypass permanent key reservations.

See the [0.3.1 to 0.4.0 upgrade procedure](https://github.com/ratchet-run/ratchet/blob/v0.4.0/website/docs/deployment/rolling-upgrades.md)
for the deployment order, retention implications, and validation steps.

## Job correctness and recovery

- Commit job completion, dependency changes, and batch accounting atomically across all
  five stores. Commit recurring job creation and schedule advancement together, preserving
  claim ownership through commit and release.
- Retain idempotency reservations after job-history deletion. Reusing a key returns its
  original job UUID, even when detailed history is gone. The reservation ledger grows with
  distinct keys, including automatically generated keys; normal history retention must
  preserve it. Keys deleted before migration cannot be reconstructed from surviving data.
- Improve lease-failure recovery, shutdown ordering, JMS reconnect behavior, invocation
  handling, archived queries, and SQL Server migration execution.
- Preserve metric tags and discover packaged OpenTelemetry beans correctly.

Jobs retain at-least-once execution semantics. Handlers must tolerate replay after crashes;
permanent idempotency prevents duplicate job creation, not repeated handler execution.

## Quarkus native images

- Register lambda serialization metadata and class resources for all application classes, including
  nested, local, and anonymous submitters. Application submission no longer depends on how the
  scheduler is obtained. Including application bytecode increases native image size.
- Preserve submitter discovery and `@RegisterJobSubmitter` for indexed dependency libraries.
  Both method references and inline lambdas require native registration.
- Derive the recurring invocation descriptor and native reflection metadata from the same method.
  Failed recurring registration remains incomplete and uses the managed retry budget; inline
  registration failures propagate to startup.

## Performance

- Support MySQL's default `REPEATABLE READ` isolation alongside `READ COMMITTED`, with
  contention fixes for claims, recurring work, and leases. Switching isolation levels is
  not required to use these improvements.
- Add priority-ordered claim indexes across SQL stores, cache lambda parsing, and avoid
  unchanged completion writes and unnecessary signal-lease operations.
- Add repeatable fixed-work load comparisons and multi-node MySQL validation. Published
  measurements describe the tested workload and hardware; they are not throughput guarantees.

No database tuning or application-server configuration change is required for the performance
improvements. Apply the schema migrations and coordinated upgrade described above.
